IMiC intervention effects on human milk: online resource Overview This online resource accompanies Dailey-Chwalibóg, Mertens et al. (2026), “Nutritional interventions’ impacts on human milk: three trials in low-resource settings”, from the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium. It holds the full results tables, interactive views of the estimates, and analyses that are not in the article. Section Contents 1 Baseline characteristics by trial and arm 2 All milk components analyzed; their distributions by trial, visit, and arm 3 Effects by maternal BMI 4 Effects on the microbiome, untargeted proteome, and untargeted metabolome 5 Component metadata; effects on each targeted milk component, with an interactive explorer 6 Effects on nutrient deficiency 7 Effects on change between visits 8 Unadjusted and native-unit effects (Table S1), treatment-arm prediction, principal-component scores, infant growth 9 Pathway and enrichment analyses (Tables S2–S7), with an interactive explorer 10 Maternal and infant blood in MISAME-III (Tables S8–S11) Estimates and plots Effects are average treatment effects (ATEs) estimated by targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE) with adjustment for baseline covariates, in standard deviations of each component’s study- and visit-specific z-score unless a table gives native units. Q is the Benjamini–Hochberg FDR-adjusted P value, computed within outcome group, study, and visit. In volcano plots, points with Q ≥ 0.05 are black (squares if P < 0.05), and points with Q < 0.05 take the color and symbol of their component category; the gray line marks P = 0.05 and the green line the FDR threshold of each panel. In forest plots of randomized arms, each arm has its own color and the symbol marks significance: open circle P ≥ 0.05, open triangle P < 0.05, filled circle Q < 0.05. Hover over a point for its values. Tables can be searched, sorted, and filtered by column. Data files The complete versions of the supplementary tables printed in part, as CSV files: table_s1_primary_secondary_native_units_wide.csv: Table S1, one row per trial, visit, and outcome: both arms side by side, with the native-unit ATE, 95% CI, P, and Q (627 rows; Section 8.2.2) table_s1_primary_secondary_native_units.csv: Table S1, one row per trial, visit, outcome, and arm: sample size, adjusted mean, and raw distribution (1,254 rows; Section 8.2.2) targeted_metabolites_native_units.csv: native-unit arm means and effects for the 581 targeted metabolites, one row per trial, visit, and metabolite (3,911 rows; Section 8.2.1) table_s3_tertiary_msea_full.csv: Table S3, targeted-metabolome MSEA, all rows (463 rows; Section 9.2) table_s6_mummichog_full.csv: Table S6, untargeted-metabolome Mummichog enrichment, pathways with P < 0.05 (505 rows; Section 9.4) table_s7_proteomics_go_full.csv: Table S7, proteome GO Biological Process enrichment, terms with P < 0.05 and Storey q < 0.20 (182 rows; Section 9.5) How to cite Cite the article, and cite this online resource by the DOI of its archive, 10.5281/zenodo.22104233, which also holds the analysis code. Source for this site: https://github.com/amertens/IMiC-intervention-effects-supplement Analysis code: https://github.com/amertens/IMiC-intervention-effects-public Trial registrations (ClinicalTrials.gov): IMiC NCT05119166; MISAME-III NCT03533712; Mumta-LW NCT03564652; ELICIT NCT03268902

Section 4 Exploratory high-dimensional outcomes: microbiome, untargeted proteomics, untargeted metabolomics This section covers human milk components that were designated as exploratory outcomes: the milk microbiome (α-diversity and individual taxa), untargeted proteomics, and untargeted metabolomics. 4.1 Microbiome 4.1.1 α-diversity Effects on z-scored observed richness and Shannon diversity, pooled and then by randomized arm. 4.1.2 Individual microbial features Per-taxon effects, pooled intervention vs. control. 4.2 Untargeted proteomics Per-protein effects, pooled intervention vs. control, in the dyads with proteomics. ELICIT is not included because its proteome samples came only from the control and azithromycin arms. The plot shows the 2,000 estimates with the smallest P, of 3,001; the table lists all of them. 4.3 Untargeted metabolomics Per-feature effects, pooled intervention vs. control, for about 97,000 features across trials, visits, and ionization modes. The plot shows the 5,000 estimates with the smallest P, of 353,656; the table lists the features with Q < 0.10.

Section 5 Adjusted intervention effects on individual milk components Covariate-adjusted effects on each primary, secondary, and tertiary milk component, by trial and visit, for the pooled intervention arms and for each randomized arm vs. control. In the tables, ATE is the effect in SD units and ATE_unscaled in native units, both with 95% CIs; perc_imp is the difference between the intervention and control means as a percentage of the control mean; pval_adj is FDR-adjusted within outcome group, trial, and visit; pval_adj_global is adjusted across all trials and visits of an outcome group; and asterisks mark P or Q below 0.05, 0.01, and 0.001. 5.1 Primary and secondary component metadata Primary and secondary components by outcome class, with the trials that measured each. 5.2 Targeted-metabolite metadata The targeted metabolites (Biocrates MxP Quant 500 panel) by compound class, with the trials that measured each. 5.3 Interactive effect explorer Every primary, secondary, and tertiary effect as a volcano plot, forest plot, or table, in SD or native units, filtered by trial, visit, and contrast. The app runs R in the browser, so the first load takes a moment. Open it in a new tab. 5.4 Macronutrients 5.5 Micronutrients (including fat-soluble vitamins) 5.6 B-vitamins 5.7 Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) 5.8 Bioactive proteins 5.9 Targeted metabolites (tertiary outcomes) Selecting points in the volcano plot (box or lasso select) filters the table beneath it, and the menus filter both. effects-on-human-milk-nutrient-deficiency.html
Section 6 Effects on human milk nutrient deficiency

Section 6 Effects on human milk nutrient deficiency Relative risks (RRs) of nutrient deficiency, pooled intervention vs. control, estimated by TMLE within each trial and visit. A sample is deficient when its concentration is below the 10th percentile of the age-specific reference distribution from the Mothers, Infants, and Lactation Quality (MILQ) study; RR < 1 means less deficiency with the intervention. nY of N samples were deficient. Components with fewer than five deficient samples in a trial and visit were not analyzed. Q (pval_adj) is FDR-adjusted within visit and outcome group.

Section 8 Sensitivity analyses and additional outputs 8.1 Unadjusted intervention effects 8.2 Unscaled (natural-unit) intervention effects 8.3 Treatment-arm prediction 8.4 Principal-component scores 8.5 Infant growth

Section 8 Sensitivity analyses and additional outputs 8.1 Unadjusted intervention effects TMLE estimates without covariate adjustment, each randomized arm vs. control. 8.2 Unscaled (natural-unit) intervention effects Adjusted effects in each component’s native units, for example g/100 mL for macronutrients, µg/L or mg/L for micronutrients, and nmol/mL for HMOs, pooled intervention vs. control. 8.2.1 Targeted metabolites (tertiary, native units) For all 581 targeted metabolites, in µM: control and intervention means, the ATE and 95% CI, percent change, native-unit P and Q, and the standardized ATE and Q (targeted_metabolites_native_units.csv). 8.2.2 Table S1 Table S1 in full, in the two formats of its data files: long, one row per trial, visit, outcome, and arm, with the sample size, the adjusted mean and 95% CI, and the raw mean, SD, median, and quartiles in native units; and wide, one row per trial, visit, and outcome, with the arms side by side and the native-unit ATE, 95% CI, P, and Q. 8.3 Treatment-arm prediction Cross-validated AUC (CV-AUC) of SuperLearner models that predict randomized arm from each class of milk components, or from all classes together, by trial, arm, and visit; 0.5 is chance. 8.4 Principal-component scores Effects on the first principal component (PC1) of each class of milk components, pooled intervention vs. control, then by randomized arm. 8.5 Infant growth Adjusted effects on infant length-for-age (LAZ) and weight-for-length (WLZ) z-scores in the IMiC subsample of each trial, each randomized arm vs. control, at birth (MISAME-III only) and at 3 and 6 months.

Section 9 Reproducible pathway and enrichment analyses 9.1 Interactive pathway explorer 9.2 Targeted-metabolome enrichment (Table S3) 9.3 Pathways enriched on both metabolomics platforms 9.4 Untargeted-metabolome Mummichog enrichment (Table S6) 9.5 Proteome Gene Ontology enrichment (Table S7)

Section 9 Reproducible pathway and enrichment analyses Pathway and enrichment analyses of the milk effects in Sections 4 and 5, run offline for each trial, visit, contrast, and direction of effect, with the features at P < 0.05 as input. Negative enrichment ratios mark down-regulated pathways. 9.1 Interactive pathway explorer Every enrichment table in the supplementary materials (Tables S2–S7), including the arm-stratified runs, as a dot plot and table, filtered by analysis, trial, and visit. The app runs R in the browser, so the first load takes a moment. Open it in a new tab. 9.2 Targeted-metabolome enrichment (Table S3) Table S3 in full: over-representation of the SMPDB small-molecule and lipid metabolite sets among the targeted metabolites, computed in MetaboAnalystR against the whole measured human metabolome as background (table_s3_tertiary_msea_full.csv). fdr_native is the Benjamini–Hochberg FDR that MetaboAnalystR reports for each run. 9.3 Pathways enriched on both metabolomics platforms Pathways with Q < 0.05 in the targeted (Table S3) or untargeted (Table S5) enrichment and P < 0.05 in the other, listing every trial, visit, contrast, and direction with P < 0.05 on either platform. 9.4 Untargeted-metabolome Mummichog enrichment (Table S6) Table S6 in full: Mummichog pathway enrichment of the untargeted milk features, matched to the human_mfn network at 10 ppm, by trial, visit, contrast, direction, and ionization mode, for the pathways with P < 0.05 (table_s6_mummichog_full.csv). FDR is Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted within each run. 9.4.1 Putative feature annotations Mass-based putative names (MSI level 3) of the FDR-significant untargeted milk features. 9.5 Proteome Gene Ontology enrichment (Table S7) Table S7 in full: over-representation of Gene Ontology Biological Process terms among the proteins with P < 0.05, using clusterProfiler::enricher with each measured UniProt protein counted once and all proteins measured in the trial and contrast as background, for the terms with P < 0.05 and Storey q < 0.20 (table_s7_proteomics_go_full.csv). fdr is Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted. The second table repeats the terms with Q < 0.05 with the contributing UniProt accessions.
cross-compartment-analyses-in-maternal-and-infant-blood.html

Section 10 Cross-compartment analyses in maternal and infant blood 10.1 Effects in each blood compartment 10.2 Concordance between compartments 10.3 Milk and maternal-blood proteomes 10.4 Acylcarnitine feature at m/z 286.202 10.5 Features increased in two or more compartments 10.6 Pathway direction and chemical classes

Section 10 Cross-compartment analyses in maternal and infant blood Intervention effects in the MISAME-III subset with maternal plasma, maternal and infant dried-blood microsample (VAMS) metabolomics, and maternal blood proteomics, and their comparison with milk. MISAME-III randomized prenatal and postnatal BEP in a 2 × 2 design: control (IFA/IFA), prenatal only (BEP/IFA), postnatal only (IFA/BEP), and both (BEP/BEP). Effects are covariate-adjusted TMLE estimates within each dataset (SD units). Because the platforms measure on different scales, compartments are compared only by the direction of their effects. Names of untargeted features are putative (mass-based, MSI level 3). Visit codes: tri3 third trimester, incl enrollment, acco birth, pn12 1–2 months postpartum, pn34 3–4 months, pn56 5–6 months. 10.1 Effects in each blood compartment The number of FDR-significant features by compartment, visit, contrast, and direction, and the putative names of those features. Per-feature results for all features are too large to include. 10.2 Concordance between compartments Agreement in direction of BEP-responsive features between compartment pairs. Features were matched across platforms by mass within ionization mode, at ±25 ppm between the two measured masses; maternal and infant postnatal VAMS share one feature catalogue and are matched by identifier. Mass-only matches can pair different molecules of the same mass. The tables give agreement among significant features, rank-based measures that use all features (rank–rank hypergeometric overlap, weighted correlation, directional GSEA), and the sensitivity of the matching to its tolerance. 10.3 Milk and maternal-blood proteomes Proteome effects in milk and maternal blood matched by UniProt accession: 302 comparisons of 215 proteins with the immunodepleted or untreated (naive) maternal-blood assay. 10.4 Acylcarnitine feature at m/z 286.202 Blood effects of the features at m/z 286.202 (putatively octenoylcarnitine, an isobaric-ambiguous annotation), then the mass and retention-time evidence for the annotation and the comparison with the acylcarnitines measured on the targeted panel. 10.5 Features increased in two or more compartments BEP-up features increased in at least two of milk, maternal blood, and infant blood, linked by shared feature identifier (maternal and infant postnatal VAMS), identical putative name, or same-mode mass (±25 ppm), with their effect in each compartment and visit and whether they were detected in the BEP supplement (18 replicates on the same platform, ±25 ppm). 10.6 Pathway direction and chemical classes Mummichog pathway enrichment of the blood features, which does not use the direction of effects, and binomial sign tests that give each pathway a direction from the signs of its mapped features’ effects. Then chemical-class over-representation among BEP-responsive blood features by direction of effect (Fisher exact test; Table S9 prints the rows with P < 0.05).
